clue.text: Means of settling European collection of laws

parts.note: COD, cash on delivery, is a way of settling a bill

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a way to resolve disputes over a body of EU legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means of settling' looks like part of the definition but supplies COD, cash on delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a systematic body of laws, such as a penal or civil code.

clue.text: Two thousand just supporting company as a rule

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath, so the thousands and just go below company

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them
only means just, as in 'just one'

explanation.surface: Two thousand people merely backing a firm is the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' looks like a link but is the order signal: in a down entry the supporter sits below.
explanation.definitionFit: Commonly means usually or ordinarily, which is what 'as a rule' says.

clue.text: Iron out the wrinkles and cut back

definitions.meaning: read playfully as the answer: to remove creases
to reduce or lessen in amount

explanation.surface: Smooth the problems away and make some economies.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as de-crease it means remove creases; normally it means reduce or lessen.

clue.text: Minor international journal chasing advance payments

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the journal and international come after the payments

parts.note: subs are advances on wages, or subscriptions paid ahead
a diary is a daily journal

explanation.surface: A lesser global magazine is pursuing money paid upfront.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsidiary means secondary or of lesser importance, a close synonym for minor.

clue.text: Practice found in mounting Pegasus

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means going upwards, so the hidden letters are read in reverse
found in says the letters sit inside the word Pegasus

explanation.surface: Riding the winged horse of myth turns out to be customary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' means climbing upward, so the letters in Pegasus are read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the habitual way something is done.

clue.text: Small boy full of strange ideas for a dish

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the small boy holds the next letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters of ideas are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little lad brimming with weird notions about food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small boy' tempts as SID, a boy's name, but splits into two pieces so that 'full of' wraps the rearranged ideas (IDESA).
explanation.definitionFit: A side salad is a small dish served alongside a main course.

clue.text: Stopped working — soon told we'd failed

indicators.note: failed suggests things went wrong, so the letters of soon told we'd are rearranged

explanation.surface: A workforce halts work after hearing their venture has collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes workers putting down their tools, i.e. ceasing work or going on strike.

clue.text: Answer before more sensible revolutionary rings

indicators.note: before puts the answer letter ahead of the next piece
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for more sensible is read backwards

parts.note: saner means more sensible

explanation.surface: A response coming ahead of a calmer rebel's.
explanation.definitionFit: Arenas are rings, as in boxing or circus rings where contests take place.

clue.text: Agreeable types succeeded in scattering enemy

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
scattering means dispersing, so the letters of enemy are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Compliant soldiers managed to disperse the foe.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged enemy, YEMEN, happens to be a country; S for succeeded is genealogy shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who agree with whatever their boss says.

clue.text: Many must go without any service staff

indicators.note: the word Many has to do without the letters of the word any that follow, leaving a single letter

parts.note: an ace is a service in tennis that the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: A complaint that a large group of waiters must manage without any help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service staff' reads as one phrase meaning waiters, but 'service' gives ACE and 'staff' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of authority.

clue.text: Clans without protection — depressing experiences for lairds, perhaps

indicators.note: the outer letters of Clans act as its shell, so stripping that protection leaves the inside

parts.note: downers are depressing or dispiriting experiences

explanation.surface: Scottish clans left defenceless suffer gloomy times, as Highland lairds might.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish estate owner; 'perhaps' marks the lairds as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairds are an example: Scottish lords who own large estates of property.

clue.text: Completed fitting — not before time!

parts.note: something over is finished or completed
due means fitting or proper, as in due respect

explanation.surface: A clothes fitting finally finished, and about time too.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'not before time!' says something arrived late, which is what overdue means.

clue.text: Almost put off Victoria, say — that's anathema!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for put off goes

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
Victoria is a London railway station, an example of a station

explanation.surface: Nearly deterred by the Queen: some find her abhorrent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims DETER to DETE; Victoria is a major London rail terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something intensely loathed, and detestation is that intense loathing.

clue.text: Leak? Refer to hotel employee

parts.note: see, as in 'see page 4', means refer to
a page is a boy who runs errands in a hotel

explanation.surface: A guest reporting a dripping pipe is told to take it up with hotel staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow escape of liquid through gaps, i.e. a leak.

clue.text: Go mad and gamble away everything, keeping hold of power

indicators.note: keeping hold of means the gambling phrase holds the next piece within it

parts.note: to lose the lot is to gamble away everything you have
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A gambler goes crazy and bets everything while clinging on to control.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's grip on reason is an idiom for going mad, as is 'flip'.

clue.text: Develop complex

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to expand on in more detail
as an adjective, intricate and detailed

explanation.surface: A short instruction to build something intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means expand in detail; as an adjective it means intricate or detailed.

clue.text: Chap with one pen having many features

parts.note: a chap is a man
I is the Roman numeral one
a fold is a pen for sheep

explanation.surface: A man owning one versatile writing pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is an enclosure for animals, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means many and various, with numerous parts or aspects.

clue.text: Flood in a French court

parts.note: un is the French for a
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A deluge in a French courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' is a verb meaning woo, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood or overwhelm with water.

clue.text: Corrupt antagonist will accept Democrat could profit

indicators.note: will accept means the rearranged letters take the next piece inside them
corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters of antagonist are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A crooked opponent will take a bribe from a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'antagonist' has the same ten letters as the answer bar one; 'Corrupt' rearranges them to STANTOGAIN before the D goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set to gain is an idiom for being in a position to profit from something.

clue.text: A father must entertain quiet hope

indicators.note: entertain means take in, so the father word holds the next letter

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A dad has to host some silent wishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or aim for something ambitious.

clue.text: Stop disheartened and study range

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so the middle letters of Stop are dropped

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: Stop feeling dejected and research your options.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is an extent or range, as in a spread of ages.

clue.text: Singer like this professional keeping a name

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the professional surrounds the next letters

parts.note: pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A singer is a pro like this one, retaining a reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest voice range.

clue.text: Defender of Italian wine kept in bond, for the most part

indicators.note: kept in means the wine is placed inside the shortened bond
for the most part means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a bond, in the sense of a tie or link
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy

explanation.surface: Imported Italian wine held in a bonded warehouse, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: Wine kept 'in bond' is stored before duty is paid; here BON(D) loses its last letter and ASTI goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a stronghold, and figuratively a defender of a principle or cause.

clue.text: Fail to justify faith with no end of grief

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the word for faith loses a letter

parts.note: belief means faith

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of grief

explanation.surface: Losing one's faith without any finish to sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: To belie is to fail to fulfil or justify, as when results belie the hype.

clue.text: Certain bail — even criminal accepts it

indicators.note: accepts means taking in, so the rearranged letters hold the next word
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of bail and even are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bail is assured, even when the offender admits the crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' looks like an adverb in the surface but is anagram fodder; 'criminal' rearranges bail and even to INEVABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inevitable is bound to happen, i.e. certain.

clue.text: Area to the west of channel island state

parts.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island in the English Channel

explanation.surface: A region lying west of an island in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight, off England's south coast, is not one of the Channel Islands; 'channel island' is read loosely. As printed, 'to the west of' should put A first, so the order is loose too.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a state of the US Midwest.

clue.text: Annoyed by objective and exposed to risk

indicators.note: by means next to, so the objective sits alongside

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective
angered means annoyed

explanation.surface: Irritated by a goal that leaves one vulnerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endangered is put in peril or at risk.

clue.text: Advantage obtained from inspired genius

indicators.note: obtained from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A competitive lead gained through a flash of brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a slight superiority over rivals, as in 'having the edge'.
